```plato

    //==
    // # Point-in-solid parity and fragmenting against a solid
    //
    // The two mid-level CSG services the boolean bodies compose: an even-odd
    // (crossing parity) interior test for a `PolygonSoup3D`, and the fragmenting of
    // polygons by every supporting plane of another solid. After cutting by every
    // plane of solid B, no fragment crosses a B plane, hence none crosses B's
    // boundary — so a single interior test on any interior point of the fragment
    // (its centroid) classifies the whole fragment.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_in_polygon)
    //
    // Robustness posture: exact floating point with a fixed skew probe direction
    // (the same posture as csg.js) — a probe ray is assumed to graze no edge and
    // parallel no face. Exactly coplanar faces of two solids sit on each other's
    // boundary and are not classified reliably.

    // The fixed probe direction for parity tests: an arbitrary irrational skew
    // direction (normalized (pi/6, ln 2, pi/4)), parallel to no axis-aligned
    // face and unlikely to graze an edge.
    CsgProbeDirection(_: Direction3D): Direction3D
        => Direction3D(Vector3D(Number.Pi / 6.0, Number.Ln2, Number.Pi / 4.0).Normalize);

    // True when the ray from `q` along `direction` strikes the polygon: it
    // crosses the supporting plane at a non-negative parameter, at a point
    // inside the ring. Grazing hits exactly on the ring boundary are not
    // classified reliably (exact-float posture above).
    RayHits(p: Polygon3D, q: Point3D, direction: Direction3D): Boolean
    {
        var hit = Ray3D(q, direction).Intersect(p.SupportingPlane);
        return hit.Hit && p.Points.PlanarPolygonContains(p.Normal.Vector, hit.Point);
    }

    // True when `q` is inside the solid, by even-odd parity: the probe ray from
    // `q` crosses the boundary an odd number of times. Points on the boundary
    // itself are not classified reliably.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_in_polygon
    Contains(s: PolygonSoup3D, q: Point3D): Boolean
        => s.Polygons
            .Map(f => f.RayHits(q, Direction3D.CsgProbeDirection) ? 1 : 0)
            .Reduce(0, (acc, c) => acc + c)
            .IsOdd;

    // The supporting planes of the solid's polygons, one per polygon, in order.
    Planes(s: PolygonSoup3D): Array<Plane>
        => s.Polygons.Map(f => f.SupportingPlane);

    // One cutting plane applied to every current fragment.
    CutByPlane(fragments: Array<Polygon3D>, pl: Plane, tolerance: Number): Array<Polygon3D>
        => fragments.FlatMap(f => f.SplitByPlane(pl, tolerance));

    // The pieces of one polygon after cutting by every plane in turn: a
    // plane-arrangement subdivision of the polygon, so no piece crosses any of
    // the planes. O(count^2) pieces in the worst case, not 2^count.
    FragmentAgainst(p: Polygon3D, planes: Array<Plane>, tolerance: Number): Array<Polygon3D>
        => planes.Reduce([p], (fragments, pl) => fragments.CutByPlane(pl, tolerance));

    // Every polygon of the solid, each cut by every plane.
    Fragments(s: PolygonSoup3D, planes: Array<Plane>, tolerance: Number): Array<Polygon3D>
        => s.Polygons.FlatMap(f => f.FragmentAgainst(planes, tolerance));

    //==
    // # Deformation body for the polygon-soup solid
    //
    // The IDeformable3D obligation of PolygonSoup3D (`solids.types.plato`):
    // every face polygon deformed vertex-wise. The soup's convex-planar invariant
    // survives affine mappings only; after a nonlinear mapping the clipping bodies
    // see each ring through its best-fit plane (the same control-point decay as
    // `brep.library.plato`), so re-tessellate first when exactness matters.

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: every polygon deformed vertex-wise.
    Deform(self: PolygonSoup3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): PolygonSoup3D
        => PolygonSoup3D(self.Polygons.Map(p => p.Deform(mapping)));
}
```
